cards.explanation: The answer is Egypt. The angel says, “Take the Child and His mother and flee to Egypt.” Joseph gets the whole plan in a dream, and the place is named right there, friends. No guessing and no wrong turns, just get up and go.

The answer is False. The angel says Herod is going to search for the Child “…to kill Him.” Herod, the king (Matthew 2:1), had told the Magi he wanted to worship Him (Matthew 2:8). The angel gives Joseph the truth, and Joseph hears it in the middle of a dream.

The answer is by night. Joseph gets up, takes the Child and His mother, and withdraws to Egypt while it's dark. Me, I once waited for a more convenient time to start a batch and the dough sat there for a week, friends. Joseph just moves.

The word is death. Joseph stayed in Egypt until the death of Herod. Matthew then says this fulfilled what the Lord had spoken through the prophet: “Out of Egypt I called My Son.” The family stays put until that point.

The word is rage. Matthew says Herod saw he had been outwitted by the Magi and “…he was filled with rage.” That's a big word, and Matthew picked it. The orders he sends in that same verse are the heavy part of this story.

The answer is the time he learned from the Magi. Herod acted “…according to the time he had learned from the Magi.” Earlier he had called the Magi in secret and found out from them the exact time the star appeared (Matthew 2:7). That's where the age came from, friends.

The answer is True. Matthew quotes Jeremiah: “…Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted, because they are no more.” I think this one hurts, friends. It's a heavy part of the story, and Matthew doesn't skip it.
The word is Israel. The angel says, “Take the Child and His mother and go to the land of Israel…” Joseph is in Egypt when the dream comes. Now he knows which way to point the family.

The reason is that those seeking the Child's life are dead. The angel says, “…for those seeking the Child’s life are now dead.” Herod's death is the point where the angel sends Joseph home. Back in Matthew 2:13, Joseph heard to stay in Egypt until the angel tells him, and now the word is go.

The answer is that he's afraid to go there. Joseph learns that Archelaus, Herod's son, is reigning in Judea in place of his father, and he is afraid to go there. Matthew gives us that fear straight from the text, friends. And then comes another dream.

The answer is True. Matthew says Joseph was “…warned in a dream…” and then he withdrew to the district of Galilee. That's the third dream in the passage, after the two where an angel of the Lord appears. And Joseph acts on this one too.

The answer is Nazareth. Joseph went and lived in a town called Nazareth, in the district of Galilee. Matthew then says what was spoken through the prophets was fulfilled: “He will be called a Nazarene.” That name goes with the town where the family lands, friends.
